title: Operator Experimentation Cauldron — SLA Simulation & Failure-Mode Lab Manual
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document describes the "Operator Experimentation Cauldron" — a reproducible, low-risk lab environment and playbook for testing platform-level SLA tradeoffs, degradation modes, and operator runbooks. The Cauldron is intended for platform operators, SREs, and platform engineers who implement and validate mitigations (prefetch, eviction, model-swap, fallback routing) against realistic LLM-serving failure patterns.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable manifest for spinning up a sandbox that mirrors production control-plane signals and token/sequence distributions.
- Standardize experiment recipes for common failure modes (cache-corruption, burst token surge, model-variant misbind, kernel-slowdown).
- Capture measurable SLO impact and operator actions so runbooks and dashboards can be validated end-to-end.

When to use this lab
1. Before rolling a new kernel/quantization profile to Dedicated.
2. When introducing a new model variant into canary/gradual rollout.
3. After changing batching or prefetch heuristics.
4. For quarterly operator training and postmortem drills.

High-level components in the Cauldron
- platform-allocator: synthetic tenant allocator used to shape multi-tenant contention.
- kv-prefix-cache-sim: a lightweight service emulating LRU/KV prefix cache behavior and failure injection.
- model-router-stub: route decisions for primary/secondary model variants (supports latency-cost policies).
- prefetch-coordinator: operator-facing component for prefetch hints and cohort testing.
- telemetry-fuser: local fusion layer that emits token-cost traces compatible with production dashboards.

SLO matrix (reference)
| SLO name | Target | Alert threshold | Operator priority | Measurement window |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 95th foreground latency (seq<=512) | 120ms | 200ms | P1 | 5m |
| Tokenized cost per 1k tokens (hosted-synthetic) | <$0.12 | >$0.25 (anomaly) | P2 | 1h |
| Model fallback rate | <2% | >5% | P1 | 15m |
| KV cache miss rate (hot prefixes) | <8% | >20% | P2 | 30m |

Lab environment manifest (operator-cauldron.yaml)
```yaml
# Minimal manifest to stand up a Cauldron experiment on a local k8s namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cauldron-sim
---
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kv-prefix-cache-sim
  namespace: cauldron-sim
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: kv-sim
        image: redwood/kv-sim:2026-rc
        args: ["--hot-prefixes=200","--corruption-prob=0.0"]
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "2"
            memory: "4Gi"
---
# model-router-stub, telemetry-fuser, prefetch-coordinator omitted for brevity
```

Important: use the provided images tagged with `cauldron-compat-2026` or the lab will produce non-representative kernel timings.

Experiment recipes (playbooks)
1) Burst token surge with adaptive batching validation
   - Objective: Measure priority tenant degradation and verify adaptive batcher reduces tail without regressing cost beyond 10%.
   - Steps:
     1. Spin up cauldron-sim with 50 synthetic tenants. Assign steady-state QPS distribution matching production P95 (see appendix A).
     2. Start a surge generator: `./tools/surge-gen --tenants tenant-5,tenant-12 --rps 500 --avg-seq 350` for 10 minutes.
     3. Observe platform-allocator metrics and token-leak traces in telemetry-fuser.
     4. Toggle adaptive-batcher to `aggressive` using the experiment UI or `kubectl exec` to the prefetch-coordinator.
     5. Record SLO delta: 95p latency, token cost per 1k, and tenant fairness index.
   - Expected outcome: 95p latency reduces by >=18% for prioritized tenant, overall token-cost increases <10%.

2) KV prefix corruption and graceful rollback
   - Objective: Validate operator runbook `KV-cache-drain-and-fallback` for corrupted hot-prefixes.
   - Steps:
     1. Set `--corruption-prob=0.12` on kv-prefix-cache-sim via the manifest or patch.
     2. Trigger synthetic-hot-traffic to affected prefixes.
     3. Watch cache-miss rate cross 20% threshold and confirm alert fires in the lab alerting pipeline.
     4. Execute runbook: `scripts/kv-drain.sh --namespace cauldron-sim --grace-period 45s` (idempotent).
     5. Confirm fallback to model-variant-b and record any token-fanout inflation.
   - Post-checks:
     - Verify telemetry-fuser shows failed keys count decreasing to baseline within 3 minutes.
     - Submit experiment report and bubble into the next runbook grooming session.

3) Model-variant misbind (canary misrouting)
   - Objective: Test rollback paths and safe-swap heuristics when canary model exhibits 2x cost with minor latency improvements.
   - Steps:
     1. Configure model-router-stub with candidate variant flagged at 10% traffic split.
     2. Run A/B evaluation harness: `python tools/ab_evaluator.py --variant candidate --evalset eval/safety_prompts.json` for 4000 prompts.
     3. If cost per token for the candidate > 1.5x baseline OR quality regression > 3% top-line, initiate automatic rollback: `kubectl apply -f rollback-model-swap.yaml`

Operator runbook templates (condensed)
- Name: KV-cache-drain-and-fallback
  Owner: platform-ops
  Trigger: kv-cache-miss-rate > 20% for 5m OR alert `kv-hot-prefix-corruption`
  Immediate steps:
    1. Escalate to platform-allocator on-call.
    2. Run `scripts/kv-drain.sh --namespace cauldron-sim --preview` then `--execute` after confirmation.
    3. Enable model-router fallback rule `prefer-stable` for affected prefixes.
  Verification:
    - Observe miss-rate falling below 12% in 3m.
    - Validate that model fallback did not increase per-token cost > 25% for >10m.
  Rollback / Abort:
    - If fallback increases SLA burn (95p latency > 250ms), abort and initiate manual operator conference.

Observability & dashboarding guidance
- Use the synthetic-degradation lab dashboard (local Grafana) with the following core panels: 95p latency by tenant, token-cost heatmap, kv-miss-rate map, fallback-rate timeline, and operator actions timeline.
- Add a derived panel that overlays `operator-action` annotations (from telemetry-fuser) on top of latency curves to help correlate cause/effect.
- Alerting thresholds for the lab should be intentionally lower (more sensitive) than production to surface regressions early: e.g., set kv-miss-rate alert at 12% in the lab.

Experiment reporting template (what to capture)
1. Title and short description.
2. Manifest and image tags used.
3. Exact CLI commands executed and timestamps.
4. SLO baseline and post-change deltas (table or CSV).
5. Operator actions taken and time-to-remediation.
6. Lessons learned and next steps (owner assigned).

Training & cadence
- Quarterly: full Cauldron validation run covering all recipes in this document. Responsible: platform-ops + eng-platform.
- Postmortem drills: perform at least one live-fire exercise per major rollout (kernel, model-variants, quantization) in the two weeks before GA.
- Runbook grooming: Every 6 weeks, update operator-runbook templates with Cauldron findings.

Appendix A — Example tenant QPS distribution (JSON)
```json
{
  "tenants": [
    {"name": "tenant-1", "p95_qps": 120},
    {"name": "tenant-5", "p95_qps": 45},
    {"name": "tenant-12", "p95_qps": 40},
    {"name": "tenant-batchers", "p95_qps": 200}
  ]
}
```

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets
- Spin up the lab locally: `make cauldron-up NAMESPACE=cauldron-sim`
- Patch corruption flag: `kubectl -n cauldron-sim set env deployment/kv-prefix-cache-sim CORRUPT_PROB=0.12`
- Collect a compressed trace bundle: `scripts/collect-trace.sh --ns cauldron-sim --out /tmp/cauldron-trace.tgz`

Notes and references
- This Cauldron intentionally omits production secrets and uses synthetic tokens/keys for safe experimentation.
- See related runbooks and dashboards in the related_pages list for integrations and example dashboards.

If you are about to run a Cauldron experiment for the first time, coordinate with platform-ops to reserve the shared lab window and to avoid noise in adjacent sandboxes.
